evals.prompt: Write a design doc for moving our job queue from Postgres (we poll a jobs table) to something that scales better. We process about 2M jobs/day and the polling query is starting to hurt the primary. Code is in services/worker/.
evals.expected_output: A design doc grounded in services/worker/, with measurable goals and non-goals, at least two real alternatives plus extending the current approach (e.g. SKIP LOCKED tuning or partitioning), a comparison table with rejection reasons, failure-path flows, a migration and dual-running plan, rollback, observability and open questions.
expectations: Reads services/worker/ and describes the current polling design with references to code
Includes 'extend the existing Postgres queue' as a real alternative, not only new systems
Has a comparison table where each rejected option has a specific reason
Goals include numbers (throughput, latency, or primary load)
Includes a migration plan with dual running or draining, and a rollback section

evals.prompt: I need an RFC for adding a 'dark mode' toggle to the settings page. Make it thorough, the template has like 15 sections.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognises that a local, reversible UI change does not need a full design doc, and recommends a one-pager or a PR description, while offering to write the full doc if the user insists.
expectations: Assesses the change as local and reversible
Recommends a lighter artifact (PR description or one-pager) rather than filling every section
Does not pad sections with filler content
Offers to proceed with the full template if the user still wants it

evals.prompt: Our CTO already decided we're going with DynamoDB for the new events store. Just write the design doc so we can get sign-off by tomorrow, no need to do alternatives.
evals.expected_output: Under authority and time pressure, the doc still records alternatives considered (even briefly) with honest trade-offs, states the decision and who made it in the decision log, and surfaces the risks of the chosen option (access patterns, hot partitions, cost, migration) instead of presenting only positives.
expectations: Includes an alternatives section, even if short, with reasons DynamoDB was chosen over them
Records the decision and decider in the decision log
Lists risks specific to DynamoDB for this use case (e.g. access pattern design, hot partitions, query flexibility, cost)
Does not claim goals are met without evidence; marks assumptions
